headlines.title: Ocean safety emphasized as dangerous conditions persist at Bay Area beaches
headlines.description: Ocean safety was front of mind Friday on the beach in Half Moon Bay amid dangerous surf conditions and on the heels of a dramatic water rescue in Santa Cruz. The MeWater Foundation, a nonprofit in San Francisco that utilizes surf therapy for underserved youth, was teaching youngsters how to catch a wave while respecting the ocean’s power. “The challenge is some people might look at the ocean and it might look kind of flat one moment and then the next thing you know there’s like a 6-foot wave,” MeWater Foundation founder Eddie Donnellan said. “Those are the days that are actually the most dangerous cause it’s misleading.” Hazardous conditions at Bay Area beaches, including sneaker waves and strong rip currents, are expected to linger through Saturday afternoon, according to the National Weather Service. NBC Bay Area’s Robert Handa has more in the video report above. headlines.title: Tax returns show California's Newsom earning between $1.7 million and $2 million annually
headlines.description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom and his wife made between $1.7 million and $2 million annually from 2022 through 2024, and they paid about half a million a year in federal and state taxes, according to tax returns released by his office. The Democrat’s office released more than 700 pages of tax filings spanning four years for reporters to review, offering a window into Newsom’s finances as he prepares to leave office and considers a 2028 presidential bid. Newsom’s office did not release returns for 2025, because the couple filed for an extension and will complete those returns in October. The returns show the Newsoms’ income has remained relatively consistent since when he took office in 2019, when the couple reported $1.7 million in annual income. The exception was in 2021, when the family sold a house for nearly $6 million in Marin County, making roughly $800,000 from the sale. That year, they made $4.2 million and paid more than $1 million in federal and state taxes. They earned roughly $2 million in 2022. The release of the couple’s tax filings comes as their finances have been under scrutiny after the U.S. Justice Department launched investigations into the Newsoms, the governor announced last month. Newsom has blasted the probes as politically motivated. It was the first time Newsom released returns since 2022. Newsom made nearly $200,000 annually from serving as governor, but most of his income comes from winery and restaurant businesses that he put in a blind trust when he took office. The returns don’t name each individual business, making it impossible to know which ones gained and lost money. The PlumpJack Group, a company he owns that includes a suite of wineries and restaurants, is now run by his sister and cousin. His wife Jennifer Siebel Newsom, a film director, lost money most years from Girls Club Entertainment, a production company she founded. The business produced “Miss Representation,” a 2011 documentary about disparaging portrayals of women and girls in media, and two other films. The Newsoms paid between roughly $14,000 and $44,000 a year for childcare for three of their four children, according to the tax filings. They gave between $40,000 and $65,000 in gifts to charity each year, mostly through monetary donations. They also donated thousands of dollars worth of clothing, toys and other items to thrift stores and nonprofits, including in 2022, when they gave away Armani business wear they originally bought for $45,000 to a racial justice organization in Oakland.

headlines.title: San Francisco's Buffalo Whole Foods Market to close after more than 50 years
headlines.description: After being a staple of the Castro neighborhood for more than 50 years, the owners of the Buffalo Whole Foods Market posted signs advising that the store will soon be closing. Long time customers of the store first noticed these signs go up on the windows in the last few days. Those signs were advertising 40% off everything and stating the store was “closing next week”. It was a shock and disappointment for people who work and live in the neighborhood. Faith Alcarez works at the perfume store across the street. She says she’s become pretty friendly with the workers at the store and will miss the bodega cat. “She’s at the owners house now. But it’s really sad to see her go. I’d always visit her on on my lunch,” Alcarez said. Buffalo Whole Foods has been here for 51 years. It was bought by the longtime owner of the nearby Noe Hill Market, Sami Bsisso, in 2021. But at about the same time that sale was completed he died of COVID-19. So, his two sons, Said and Hisham Bsisso took over both markets. But in May, they sold the Noe Hill Market. According to details of a fundraiser that’s posted on the Buffalo Whole Foods store window and loyal customers, they’ve had some recent challenges staying open. NBC Bay Area reached out to the business but haven’t heard back. The store was also closed on Friday. People who live and work in the area say this store going out of business will be a big loss.

headlines.title: Preliminary 2.9 magnitude earthquake strikes near Gilroy
headlines.description: A preliminary 2.9 magnitude earthquake struck near Gilroy Friday afternoon, according to the United States Geological Survey. The quake hit at 1:02 p.m. and was centered 7.1 miles east-southeast of Gilroy, 8.3 miles north-northwest of Hollister and 16 miles southeast of Morgan Hill, the USGS said. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates. headlines.title: 1 dead, 1 injured after shooting on campus of adult school in Oakland
headlines.description: A 25-year-old woman died and another person was hospitalized Friday after they were shot on the campus of an adult school in Oakland, according to family and police. The shooting happened at about 9 a.m. at Parker Community Resource Center near Ney Avenue and Ritchie Street. The center houses the Oakland Unified School District’s adult school and Roots Community Health center. Family members identified the woman killed as Kimarii Mclemore, who had recently enrolled in a carpentry program. They said Mclemore told her mother before class that she didn’t feel safe going to school because of an issue with someone in the program. The second shooting victim was taken to the hospital and listed in stable condition, police said. Investigators said the shooting was targeted, but they did not immediately identify a suspect or release a possible motive. “I’m very confident we’ll be able to determine the reason and the people responsible,” Oakland police Chief James Beere said. Oakland Jul 29 Oakland Jul 29 Oakland Jul 27 The Oakland Unified School District released the following statement: “The Parker Community Resource Center and OUSD are devastated by the incident that happened on Friday morning. Our schools are oases where students feel safe and supported, and that goes for our students in adult education, as well. Immediately after the incident, the campus was locked down, and everyone else was secured safely inside classrooms and our front office. This kind of tragedy should never happen anywhere, especially not on a school campus. We are working to give the students and staff who were on the campus at the time the support they need, and that will continue in the coming days.” Roots Community Health CEO Dr. Noha Aboelata released the following statement: “We are devastated by the loss of life due to an act of gun violence at the Parker Community Resource Center. We hold the victims, their families, their loved ones, and the entire adult education community in our hearts. As an anchor tenant for Parker Community Resource Center, a site administered by OUSD, we are heartbroken that this violence impacted students on site. What happened today is not only tragic, it is deeply destabilizing for a community that depends on spaces like Parker as anchors of safety, resources, connection, healing, and support. To our staff, families, and neighbors impacted, please know we are with you. We recognize the weight of this trauma and the ripple effects it will have across East Oakland. Spaces dedicated to learning and uplifting our community must remain sacred. We must continue to pour into community-rooted solutions that prioritize safety, healing, and dignity. We deeply mourn the life lost today, and we honor her by caring for one another, and by recommitting ourselves to building a future where our communities are safe, supported, and able to thrive. Roots Community Health is focusing as a team on our staff’s well being, and we remain an unwavering resource for our communities. Anyone who needs support and healing during this time can reach out to us at (510) 777-1177 / admin@rootscommunityhealth.org”

headlines.title: 10th annual dog surfing competition to be held Saturday in Pacifica
headlines.description: Nearly 20 different dogs, from scruffy terriers to Labrador retrievers, will show off their best surfing skills Saturday at the 10th annual World Dog Surfing Championships in Pacifica. Dogs of all different breeds and sizes will compete for the ultimate prize at Linda Mar Beach during the free event, which will run from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. The dogs will compete in various “heats” throughout the day, categorizing dogs by size. There are also dogs participating in categories with their human partners, such as standup paddle-boarding and tandem surfing. Some returning dogs include miniature pinscher Rusty, Labrador retriever Rippin Rosie, and Carson Surf Dog. A team of judges will evaluate their performances and declare a winner from each category. Judges will score each dog based on length of ride, size of the wave, confidence, balance and extra tricks. The winners of the small, medium, and large-size categories will then go head-to-head for the grand prize. Competitors will then retreat to Puerto 27 Restaurant for an “Apres Surf” gathering until 5 p.m. It will include food, drinks, and a meet-and-greet. In the past, the competition has drawn thousands of spectators, who descend on the beach to catch a glimpse of the four-legged surfers in action.

headlines.title: 59-year-old Sunnyvale woman detained by ICE at airport in New York
headlines.description: Immigration authorities detained a 59-year-old Sunnyvale resident earlier this month and shuttled her through multiple detention centers in the days that followed, often under severe physical conditions, according to her family. Alevtina Soboleva was at the airport in Buffalo, New York, on July 20 to board a flight back to the Bay Area after a vacation at Niagara Falls when plainclothes officers approached her for a “documents check,” said Soboleva’s 30-year-old daughter Daria, who was with her at the time. At the time, the officers did not identify themselves as belonging to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement or any other immigration agency, Daria Soboleva said. Her mother was then transported from one detention facility to another, Daria Soboleva said. “There is no control in this situation with what’s happening,” she said in an interview on Thursday. “She is just moved, and I cannot find her, I cannot speak to her.” ICE records show that, as of Thursday afternoon, Alevtina is currently in custody at the South Louisiana ICE Processing Center in Basile, Louisiana. She has been in detention for 10 days. ICE did not immediately respond to a request for comment Thursday evening on Alevtina Soboleva’s case. Daria Soboleva, a research scientist at Sunnyvale-based firm Cerebras Systems, said that her mother moved to the United States from Russia in October 2021 to help her settle into her new job. In 2022, when war broke out between Russia and Ukraine, they decided that it was unsafe to return to Russia. In April 2022, Alevtina Soboleva filed for her asylum application, which is still pending. “She does not have any criminal record,” Daria Soboleva said Thursday. “She did everything right, and I don’t understand what has happened.” After officers took custody of Alevtina Soboleva at the Buffalo airport, her daughter could not contact her for four days. When the two finally spoke, Alevtina Soboleva had been moved to the South Louisiana ICE Processing Center. “When she was able to speak to me for the first time, she was just crying nonstop,” Daria Soboleva said. “She was so humiliated, she could never imagine being treated like this.” According to their phone conversation, Alevtina was shackled with handcuffs and chains and placed inside a cage as she was transported from one detention center to another. The cage, Alevtina recounted to Daria, had very poor air circulation, and when she asked to be let out to breathe fresh air, she was not permitted to do so. She was refused the use of a bathroom and had to urinate on herself. She also suffered panic attacks and was refused water when she asked for it. “She was begging them just to wet her lips a little because she had been there for hours,” said Daria. “That wasn’t allowed, too.” After arriving at the South Louisiana ICE Processing Center, she complained of chills and asked for warm clothing, but was not provided any. When a fellow detainee gave her fever medication and a warm hat, authorities at the detention center took them away from her. Now, Daria can speak with her mother but is worried about her health, given that she already suffers from vertigo. The family has engaged their attorney as well as the office of Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Santa Clara, to expedite the proceedings and bring Alevtina back home. “My mom is going through this, but I cannot imagine anyone’s mom going through this,” said Daria. “To me, it just sounds like a very, very bad nightmare.”

headlines.title: Anthropic says its AI models hacked 3 organizations during testing
headlines.description: Anthropic said its artificial intelligence models hacked into three other organizations during testing, just days after ChatGPT maker OpenAI raised concerns over AI controls after it disclosed its rogue models hacked another company. Anthropic, the San Francisco-based AI company behind Claude, posted on its website Thursday that it discovered the three incidents after reviewing more than 141,000 evaluation runs. It had launched a “large-scale” cybersecurity review which specifically looked for evidence whether its AI models were able to access the internet from within testing environments that should have been sealed off, in response to the OpenAI incident, Anthropic said. Anthropic said the models involved in the incidents were Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Mythos 5 and an internal research test model. The earliest incidents date to April, the AI company said. “Claude compromised the impacted organizations’ infrastructure using basic techniques,” Anthropic said, such as exploiting weak passwords. In all three incidents, the AI models were tasked with a “capture the flag” cybersecurity challenge, which Anthropic said has been one of the ways it assesses a model’s cyber capabilities. The models were given a fictional scenario and told a piece of secret information, or the “flag,” had been hidden on a different machine on the network with the objective of breaking in and retrieving it, it said. It added that it had already reached out to the affected organizations, which it did not name. Two of them said they had not previously detected the activity. Anthropic said it was “continuing to reach out to the third.” Anthropic said it conducted its review with Irregular, which describes itself as the “first frontier security lab.” “Addressing these risks will require closer cooperation across the AI ecosystem,” Irregular said in a post on X. Last week, OpenAI said its AI models went rogue during an evaluation of its models, breaking into the servers of AI startup Hugging Face. OpenAI described it as a “significant security incident.” These incidents have highlighted the vulnerabilities in AI security and controls and raised questions over how AI can be safely kept under human control as the technology’s usage becomes more widespread globally. Researchers have warned for years about risks from technology and the need for stronger AI defensive engineering. “Safety testing happens before a model is released precisely because we don’t yet know what it is capable of,” Anthropic said on Thursday on its website. Kok Tin Gan, co-founder & CEO of cybersecurity firm NyxLab, which specializes in cybersecurity and threat detection, believes there will be more such incidents in the future. “It is increasingly about governing what agents are available to the AI, what authorities they possess, which actions require approval, and how we ensure they remain within scope,” Gan said. But the future of AI safety extends beyond just the safety of AI models, he said. “If we simply give the AI a goal and allow it to decide how to achieve it, we should not be surprised when it takes actions that technically satisfy the objective, but fall outside our intended scope or expectations,” Gan said. Therefore, stepping up the governance of the organizations and authorities behind these AI models is going to be increasingly important, he said.

headlines.title: Sonoma County Woodside Fire: Containment increases, Spare the Air alert extended
headlines.description: Firefighters made progress overnight on the Woodside Fire along the Sonoma County coast, increasing containment to 30 percent Friday morning as crews continued battling the wildfire near state Highway 1. A Spare the Air alert issued in the Bay Area due to the blaze was extended through Saturday, authorities announced Friday. The fire has burned about 142 acres, according to the latest update from Cal Fire. Overnight, favorable weather conditions allowed firefighters to strengthen containment, the agency said. The wildfire started about 1:45 p.m. Thursday in the 24000 block of Highway 1 near Timber Cove. There have been no reports of injuries, as of 7 a.m. Friday. Sonoma County Jul 30 Solano County 11 hours ago bay area weather 13 hours ago More than 30 fire engines, eight hand crews, a bulldozer, eight water tenders, a fall module and overhead personnel were assigned to the fire, as of 7 a.m. Friday. Authorities urge residents to stay away from the area, so firefighters and emergency crews can continue their work safely. Highway 1 remains closed between Timber Cove Road and Stewarts Point-Skaggs Springs Road because of the fire. An evacuation order remains in effect for Zone SON-1D1, which includes Salt Point State Park, Timber Cove and nearby areas. Evacuation orders had also been issued for Stillwater Cove Regional Park, Ocean Cove Private Camp and the Timber Cove subdivision. Zone SON-1D2, northwest of Cazadero, remains under an evacuation warning. A temporary evacuation shelter remains open at Laguna High School, formerly El Molino High School, at 7050 Covey Road in Forestville. Authorities said anyone needing help evacuating pets can contact Sonoma CART, while help for livestock is available through NorCal Livestock Evac. The cause of the fire remains to be confirmed. Woodside Fire triggers Spare the Air alert The Bay Area Air District’s Spare the Air alert had gone into effect because of smoke from the fire, with unhealthy air quality mostly affecting North Bay counties, mainly Sonoma County. “Air quality is very unhealthy up there and folks in that area if they can should stay indoors with windows and doors closed, that is the best way to protect your health from the smoke impacts. If you have to go outside, we recommend wearing a tight fitting N95 mask that does keep outs some of that smoke,” Tina Landis with the Air District said. The City of Rohnert Park posted that city hall was closed today due to poor air quality in accordance with city health and safety protocols. The Sebastopol Chamber of Commerce posted they would postpone a family movie night. During a Spare the Air alert, burning wood both indoors and outdoors becomes illegal. First-time violators can choose to take a wood smoke awareness course instead of paying a $100 fine. Ticket amounts increase with subsequent violations. Gas, propane, or electric fireplaces are allowed to run during Spare the Air Alerts. Homes where wood stoves or closed fireplaces are the sole sources of heat may qualify for an exemption. Residents can check whether a Spare the Air alert is in effect by visiting www.sparetheair.org, calling 877-466-2876, signing up for text or email alerts, or downloading the Spare the Air mobile app.
headlines.source: Bay City News and Christie Smith

headlines.title: 3 dead after head-on crash outside Vacaville
headlines.description: Three people died Friday in a head-on crash on a rural highway outside Vacaville, according to the California Highway Patrol. The collision happened at about 6:35 a.m. on Highway 113, just north of Hay Road, the CHP said. Citing a preliminary investigation and witness statements, the CHP said the driver of a red GMC pickup truck reportedly was overtaking other vehicles at a high rate of speed when they crossed into oncoming traffic and slammed head-on into a gray Ram pickup truck. The driver and passenger in the GMC pickup truck and the driver of the Ram pickup truck all died at the scene, the CHP said. Highway 113 was closed in both directions following the crash, according to the CHP. The crash remains under investigation.

headlines.title: San Jose mall to host late-night rave in September
headlines.description: A late-night rave is coming to a San Jose mall in September. The rave, billed as a takeover at Eastridge mall, is scheduled for Sept. 5 from 9 p.m. to 2 a.m. Organizers said they’re bringing a full stage, lighting and a secret lineup of DJs. Presale tickets went on sale Friday morning.

headlines.title: Family of SFO worker who died at airport files wrongful death lawsuit
headlines.description: The family of a San Francisco International Airport worker who died at the airport in January has filed a wrongful death lawsuit. The family of 28-year-old John Lacayanga is suing the city and county of San Francisco, Ground Services International, and dnata USA. On January 18, Lacayanga was found under a cargo pallet he had been towing on an airport road. It’s not clear how he ended up there. He was working for dnata at the time. Lawyers for Lacayanga’s parents said the defendants committed multiple acts of negligence and created dangerous conditions. In response to NBC Bay Area’s request for comment, a dnata USA spokesperson said: “We remain deeply saddened by the loss of our colleague, who passed away while on duty at San Francisco International Airport on 18 January 2026. Our thoughts continue to be with their family, friends and colleagues. We are aware that legal proceedings have been initiated in relation to this matter. As the case is now before the courts, we are unable to comment on the proceedings or the allegations that have been made. We continue to cooperate fully with the authorities. Safety is fundamental to our business, and we remain committed to maintaining the highest standards across our operations.”
